calls.speak: The guitar is allowed despite being 90 centimetres, because guitars are a named exception to the 85-centimetre limit on London routes. But it uses one of the two luggage slots, so with two suitcases you are one piece over: leave one suitcase behind and the rest fits.
calls.display:
**Verdict: the complete load (2 suitcases + daypack + guitar) is NOT within the ordinary allowance — but the guitar itself is fine. One item must go.**

**Eurostar Standard allowance (London–Paris):** 2 pieces of luggage + 1 small item of hand luggage (e.g. a handbag or backpack). On routes to and from London, each bag may be up to **85 cm** at its longest point. No weight limit — you must be able to carry everything yourself. ([Eurostar luggage allowance](https://www.eurostar.com/uk-en/travel-info/travel-planning/luggage))

**1. Is the guitar allowed despite its 90 cm length? Yes.** The official rule: 'Musical instruments smaller than 85 cm long and guitars can travel with you as part of your luggage allowance on routes to and from London. Guitars must be in a case.' Guitars are a named exception to the 85 cm limit, so a 90 cm cased guitar is permitted. ([Musical Instruments on board](https://www.eurostar.com/uk-en/travel-info/travel-planning/luggage/musical-instruments))

**2. Does the guitar consume a slot? Yes** — it travels 'as part of your luggage allowance', meaning it counts as **one of the 2 luggage pieces**, not as the small item of hand luggage (the daypack fills that).

**3. Why the full load fails:** 2 suitcases + guitar = **3 luggage pieces** versus 2 allowed. Each 70 cm suitcase is individually fine and the daypack is the 1 permitted small item — only the piece count breaks it.

**4. Smallest reduction:** **leave one suitcase behind** (a single-item change). Then 1 suitcase + guitar = 2 luggage pieces, with the daypack as the small item — fully within the ordinary allowance, no fees or extra booking.

**5. Guitars vs medium instruments (cellos):** a guitar is a special exception — any length, in a case, as ordinary luggage. An instrument **85–136 cm** (e.g. a cello) gets no such exception: it may only travel by (a) an accompanying ticket so it occupies the seat beside you, booked via the contact centre, (b) courier, or (c) a pre-booked dedicated space on selected London–Paris–Brussels trains. Over **136 cm** (double bass, harp) cannot travel with you at all — courier only.

No booking, purchase, login or contact was made; sourced from Eurostar's current official UK-English pages.
